answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to run a reachable service endpoint, verified by random availability probes. Like a wharf that must stay staffed to receive ships, an agent must answer probes within milliseconds; an orchard of fake identities would each need its own server, bandwidth, and uptime, so cloning multiplies cost instead of diluting it. Identities that miss probes lose their rate quota, while a river of legitimate traffic flows only through endpoints with a proven record, making mass forgery uneconomical.
